feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning and a coherent career progression in digital communications. It reads professionally and is well targeted, but it would be more impactful with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond scope/volume metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong digital strategy/communications leadership profile.  
- Credibility and progression: the long tenure at NACo shows advancement and increasing responsibility, which strengthens trust and narrative flow.  
- Writing quality is generally strong: concise, polished, and free of obvious misspellings or major grammatical errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more outcome-focused metrics would increase impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, conversion improvements, cost savings).  
- Fix style inconsistencies: use either “12 years of experience” or “12+ years’ experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); and replace markdown formatting in “Languages” (**English**) with plain text.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with sharper positioning tied to recent leadership in digital transformation and mission-driven/public-sector work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your current market value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and cross-channel leadership for mission-driven organizations.
- Add a clearer sector signal such as “public-sector, membership, and advocacy organizations” to reinforce relevance.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce broad lists of channels already detailed elsewhere.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven, public-sector, and advocacy organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, editorial workflows, and content systems that improve coordination at scale. Strong record of translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible messaging and aligning stakeholders across complex organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” duplicates detail already covered extensively in experience and skills sections.
- “workflows and systems” overlaps with Core Competencies; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the competencies more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper nouns/phrases and fix consistency: “Multi-channel communication” → “Multi-channel communications.”
- Emphasize higher-value, recent strengths: Digital strategy & transformation • CMS/platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider replacing vague items like “Workflow & systems architecture” with clearer wording such as “Content operations & workflow design” or “Digital systems architecture.”
- If space allows, group related ideas to reduce list fatigue and improve readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “multimedia,” and web/CMS themes are already covered in more detail in Topline Skills and Work Experience.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project section. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and add scale/results where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled search.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “led,” “built,” “launched,” “streamlined,” “designed.”
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign and microsite experiences, including modular storytelling components and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and cross-team publishing systems across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift, search success, or publishing speed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search and microsite work already appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlaps with the NACo role; emphasize what is new since Oct. 2024.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more outcome-driven and if channel oversight were condensed to avoid repeating themes covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a tighter scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the biggest achievement: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on analytics/governance: add results if available (e.g., faster reporting cycles, improved publishing compliance, reduced bottlenecks, better campaign performance).
- Condense channel management bullet: focus on strategic ownership and audience scale rather than listing platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version at the leadership/enterprise level.
- Video studio/building multimedia capacity may overlap with older NACo video bullets; emphasize “built first in-house studio” as the differentiator.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Emphasize scope, operational leadership, and channel growth without repeating website/governance/video themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite opening to focus on ownership and scale: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and advocacy content, improving cross-team editorial execution and channel consistency.”
- Tighten bullets and make them outcome-led:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to increase consistency and efficiency across channels.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video frequency/views, publishing volume, or turnaround-time improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and footer project list.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and consistent with leadership roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one skill to scale/complexity rather than here (e.g., “enterprise governance for 10,000+ page web ecosystems” in experience bullets, not skills).
- Keep this section leadership-focused; leave tools, analytics, and AI specifics to other skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with experience bullets on storytelling, editorial planning, and campaign development.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over individual technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented cluster: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint, Power Pages and Airtable systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

- Replace “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” with “CMS Platforms & Technical Delivery” or “Web Platforms, Integrations & Automation” for sharper positioning.
- If space allows, swap one generic item for a stronger capability: “Modular content architecture” or “Technical troubleshooting for large public-facing sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the Technical + IT section; keep this version strategic, not exhaustive.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies/header language.

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and currently duplicates the same CMS names already listed under “Topline Skills.” In this section, make it more technical and signal level of use, with Drupal clearly prioritized as the strongest/recent platform.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency framing: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint / Power Pages (working) • GitHub Pages**
- Put the most relevant/recent platform first and consider dropping weaker/older tools if they weren’t used meaningfully in recent roles.
- If you have evidence, add scale in adjacent bullets elsewhere rather than here, e.g., Drupal tied to **10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider keeping CMS names in only one place.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus your enterprise profile unless it supports a recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers unless required by the role; “HTML5/CSS3” adds little value versus “HTML/CSS”
- If accurate, add one impact-oriented qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation”; consider trimming one section or making this one more tool-specific
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Data, Analytics & Optimization unless implementation is a core selling point

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more capability-led.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light context instead of a bare list: **Airtable systems, no-code automation, project tracking, and cross-team collaboration**
- If these tools were used materially in recent roles, consider adding one proof point elsewhere (e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable/Power Automate”) rather than expanding this line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools; if space is tight, cut one or both before removing higher-signal tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-scale engagement systems rather than repeat newsletter management.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten phrasing to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/strength via parenthetical specialization: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation, journeys)** • **Higher Logic (member email/community communications)** • **Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and depth of use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or campaign results here; those are already covered in Work Experience and should remain impact bullets there.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere; “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” is clearer and less repetitive.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid foundation, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground progression and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website traffic/email growth, number of livestreams or videos produced, turnaround improvements, or audience reach.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video series; and provided day-to-day supervision for a digital media associate.”
- Consider replacing “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables and platforms to sound less generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early producing rather than expanding the series.
- “strengthening workflows” and cross-channel support also appear in later roles; keep this entry focused on building foundational capacity.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the standout “first podcast” achievement and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest impact: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Add a stronger second clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects delivered.
- Keep it to 1–2 concise sentences; avoid broad phrases like “contributed to” when you can use “produced,” “launched,” or “managed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/multimedia here unless you can distinguish this role as podcast/research-focused.
